question: According to the unit, what is the most significant consequence of large class size for language learning?
options: Teachers are unable to write lesson plans that include grammar activities
Shared time sharply limits each learner's language production
Discipline problems increase to the point where communicative activities become impossible
Teachers lose the ability to use pair work because rooms are too crowded to rearrange
answer: Shared time sharply limits each learner's language production
anchor: each individual's opportunity to produce language shrinks to a fraction of what a smaller class would allow

question: The unit explains that displaying group work products on the classroom wall serves a purpose beyond the lesson itself. What does the unit identify as a key benefit of this practice?
options: It allows the teacher to assess all students simultaneously without circulating
It reduces the need for written homework because students have already produced a public artifact
It creates a circulation of attention among students who read and respond to each other's work
It signals to administrators that communicative tasks are being completed
answer: It creates a circulation of attention among students who read and respond to each other's work — Other groups have a reason to read and respond to work that is not their own, creating a circulation of attention that a single teacher-fronted display cannot replicate.
anchor: creating a circulation of attention that a single teacher-fronted display cannot replicate

question: The unit describes a specific risk when a teacher circulates without a plan during student work time. What is that risk?
options: The teacher will spend too long at each desk and fail to complete the lesson
Students in the front rows will feel singled out and become reluctant to participate
Unplanned circulation favors confident, front-row students
Pair work will break down because students expect the teacher to visit every pair equally
answer: Unplanned circulation favors confident, front-row students
anchor: a teacher who circulates without a plan will inevitably return to the same confident students, the same front rows

question: The unit recommends 'classroom learning systems' as the foundation of managing a large class. Define the term and give one example of such a routine from the unit.
answer: Classroom learning systems are the clear routines, expectations, and physical arrangements a teacher sets up in advance to make the class run smoothly. One example: posting the day's agenda on the board at the start of class, so students know what is coming without the teacher spending time explaining it.
anchor: clear routines, expectations, and physical arrangements a teacher sets up in advance
